details.purpose: لتسجيل تفاصيل نتيجة اختبار المُخَطَّط الطبلي
To record measurements of movement at the tympanic membrane in response to changes in air pressure in the ear canal and to infer middle ear function.
details.use:
Use to record movement of the tympanic membrane in response to various levels of air pressure, for a single ear at a time.
Use to record the interpretation all measurements to infer middle ear function for each ear, plus an overall interpretation (or tympanometric diagnosis).
All of the data elements are recorded using a single method or protocol. If, during the test, any of the protocol parameters need to be modified, then the subsequent part of the test will need to be recorded within a separate instance of the test data, using the updated protocol parameters.
details.misuse: Not to be used to record other hearing tests. Use other archetypes as appropriate, for example OBSERVATION.audiogram.

*Default, unspecified point in time or interval event which may be explicitly defined in a template or at run-time.(en)
*Description of the the shape of the tympanogram plot using Jerger categories.(en)
*A distinctive sharp peak, around atmospheric pressure (between +50 to -99 daPa), static compliance = 0.3 to 1.6cc (adults) or 0.2 to 0.9cc (children 3 – 5yrs), and normal ear canal volume.(en)
*Rounded line/no measurable peak pressure, reduced static compliance (<2cc), ear canal volume within normal range.(en)
*As for Type A, but Peak Pressure less than -99 daPa i.e., a significant negative middle ear pressure.(en)
*As for Type A but with reduced static compliance (< 0.3cc).(en)

*The right ear was tested in isolation.(en)
*The tympanogram test result, recorded per ear.(en)

*Also known as Middle Ear Pressure (MEP). It is plotted on the horizontal axis on a tympanogram.(en)
*Static compliance (SC) is the greatest amount of acoustic energy absorbed by the middle ear system (the vertical peak of the tympanic tracing).(en)
*Also known as 'Static Admittance'. It is plotted on the verical axis of a tympanogram.(en)

*An estimate of the volume of air between the probe tip and the tympanic membrane if the tympanic membrane is intact, or the volume of the ear canal and the middle ear space if the tympanic membrane is perforated. (Fowler & Shanks, 2002, p. 180).(en)
*Additional narrative about the test results and intepretation not captured in other fields.(en)
*Multiple instances of this measurement will form the basis for the graphical display of the tympanogram.(en)

*This value is typically derived from the Tympanogram curve.(en)

*This value is typically derived from the Tympanogram curve.(en)
*No test result is available for the test ear.(en)
*Record as True if the clinician was unable to record a result for the test ear.(en)
*Reason why no result is available for the test ear.(en)
*For example, patient was not co-operative; patient was not capable; ran out of time; no seal; presence of tympanic membrane perforation, impacted wax or discharge.(en)
*Clinical interpretation of all measurements for the test ear.(en)
*Coding with a terminology is preferred, where possible.(en)
*As for Type A but with increased static compliance (>1.6cc).(en)
*It is not possible to determine the exact type of middle ear function.(en)
*Overall clinical interpretation of the measurements and related findings using an tympanometer.(en)
*Coding with a terminology is preferred, where possible. This data element is effectively an tympanometric diagnosis.(en)

*Measurements are recorded after the patient has performed a toynbee manoeuvre.(en)

*The frequency of the tone emitted by the probe inserted into the test ear.(en)
*The dirction of change of pressure administered via the ear canal.(en)
*The pressure changes from positive to negative.(en)
*The pressure changes from negative to positive.(en)
*The rate of change of pressure used in tympanometry.(en)
*Method of acoustic admittance measurement used in the test.(en)

*The rate and direction of change in the air pressure in the ear canal used to obtain the tympanogram.(en)

*The pressure value in daPa at which the pressure sweep for tympanometry begins. It is a positive pressure if the direction of pressure change is descending and a negative pressure if the direction of pressure change is ascending.(en)
